text:
A: Hello, can you hear me? I'm Alison.
B: Alright, yeah, loud and clear. Darren. Nice to meet you.
A: You too. I think I saw your picture earlier, with the calendar. Is that starlings?
B: Yeah, a murmuration. Not mine, that one, it's bought, but I go and photograph them at Ham Wall, on the Levels. Season's just starting, actually.
A: Oh, how lovely. I've only seen it on the telly. Where's that, then?
B: Somerset. Near Glastonbury, sort of. I'm in Bridgwater. You?
A: Ipswich. Suffolk. Bit of a way.
B: Bit of a drive, yeah. So what do you do?
A: I'm a practice nurse at a GP surgery. Diabetes reviews, asthma, smears, jabs, that sort of thing.
B: Oh right. Proper job, that. I'm a machine operator, packaging line at a food plant. Four on, four off, days and nights.
A: Nights, oh gosh. How do you find that? I see a lot of shift workers and it does take it out of you.
B: Honestly, it wrecks me. The sleep goes for days after. And I'll be honest, I'm one of them who sits there at three in the morning on a break googling symptoms. Headache, tired, you put it in and it tells you you're dying.
A: Oh, don't do that! We see so many people who've frightened themselves on Google. Nine times out of ten it's being tired and not drinking enough water. Erm, and if you're worried, just book in, that's what we're there for, you know. Nobody minds.
B: Yeah, fair. That's what the wife says. I just don't like wasting their time.
A: You wouldn't be. Honestly. The ones who worry about wasting our time are never the ones who are.
B: (laughs) Good to know. I do look after myself a bit. Got a rowing machine in the garage, log every session on a spreadsheet.
A: A spreadsheet! That's very organised. I did couch-to-5K a few years ago and never quite kept it up. Now I just walk by the river.
B: Same, I walk the dog along the Parrett. Bruno. He's a Staffie, getting on now, bit slow. I sort of dread it, to be honest.
A: Oh, bless him. How old is he?
B: Twelve, thirteen. Had him before Alfie, my lad, was born.
A: Oh, that's hard. I've got a cat, Biscuit, ginger tom. He sits on my keyboard. He might well appear.
B: (laughs) Go on, I'll look out for him. Do you get away much?
A: Once a year with my sister. Spain or Portugal. We did a river cruise on the Douro once, I still go on about it. But I'm a terrible flyer.
B: Me too! I print everything off, boarding passes, the lot, all in a plastic wallet. Wife thinks I'm mad. Did Normandy, the beaches, researched it for months. Military history's my thing, so.
A: Oh, that must have been moving. My dad was always into all that. I'm the same with the printing, and I'm at the airport three hours early.
B: Three hours, yeah. Better than missing it.
A: Exactly. My son says, Mum, you'll be sat there for ages. And I say, yes, with a cup of tea, happily. He's about your age, actually, my son. Same sort of haircut.
B: (laughs) I'll take that. Where's he, then?
A: Colchester, with his partner. They've got a little girl now, I mind her on Fridays.
B: Nice. Alfie's eight, he's into Minecraft, I don't get it at all. I'm tiling our downstairs loo at the moment, doing it all myself, and he just wants to build houses on a screen.
A: (laughs) Well, at least he's building something. Maybe he'll take after you.
B: That's what I keep telling myself. I want him to go to university, mind —
